evidence.title: Taforalt (Grotte des Pigeons): late Iberomaurusian burials & aDNA
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS radiocarbon dates on sampled human individuals and associated Iberomaurusian necropolis layers.
evidence.summary: Seven 15,000-year-old genomes from Taforalt reveal deep pre-agricultural ancestry links combining a Levantine Natufian-like component and a sub-Saharan African genetic affinity without European Neolithic gene flow.
evidence.limits: Sampled skeletons represent one cave necropolis in northeastern Morocco rather than the entire Maghreb population.

evidence.title: Jebel Sahaba (Site 117): Late Pleistocene cemetery & violence reappraisal
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon determinations on skeletal and associated contexts near the Nile Second Cataract.
evidence.summary: Reanalysis of 61 burials documents both lethal and healed projectile traumas across repeated skirmishes or ambushes rather than one single massacre event, alongside climatic instability along the Late Pleistocene Nile.
evidence.limits: Individual bone collagen degradation leaves some individual graves less precisely dated than the cemetery envelope.

evidence.title: Gobero (Niger): Kiffian lakeside hunter-fisher-gatherer cemetery
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on human burials and paleolake shore deposits in the Ténéré Desert.
evidence.summary: Early African Humid Period lake shores at Gobero supported largely sedentary fisher-forager communities with barbed bone harpoons and distinctive burials prior to mid-Holocene arid pulses.
evidence.limits: An arid interval separates the Kiffian burials from later pastoral Tenerian occupations at the same paleolake basin.

evidence.title: Eastern Maghreb Capsian escargotières & plant use
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian radiocarbon modeling of Typical and Upper Capsian shell-midden layers across eastern Algeria and Tunisia.
evidence.summary: Early-to-Middle Holocene hunter-gatherers built dense mound middens (escargotières), gathered wild grasses including Alfa, and practiced contemporaneously overlapping bladelet traditions.
evidence.limits: Point marks a representative eastern Maghreb Capsian research corridor rather than a single excavation.

evidence.title: Nabta Playa & Bir Kiseiba: early pastoral landscapes
evidence.dateBasis: Playa basin stratigraphy and radiocarbon series; early 9th millennium cattle status remains actively debated.
evidence.summary: Seasonal lakes in Egypt’s Western Desert hosted mobile cattle-herding communities, cattle tumuli, and aligned megalithic stone circles linked to monsoon waterholes.
evidence.limits: Taxonomic identification and Southwest Asian vs. independent Northeast African origins of early Bos remains debated.

evidence.title: Takarkori (Tadrart Acacus): earliest Saharan dairying & ancient DNA
evidence.dateBasis: Direct radiocarbon dates on pastoral pottery organic residues and ~7,000-year-old human genomes.
evidence.summary: Ceramic lipid analysis documents fifth-millennium BCE milk fats, while 2025 ancient genomes from Takarkori reveal an isolated deep North African lineage that adopted herding primarily via cultural exchange rather than mass turnover.
evidence.limits: Sheltered microclimates preserve organic macromolecules better than open desert surface sites.

evidence.title: Kaf Taht el-Ghar (Morocco): Cardial Neolithic & maritime arrival
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on Early Neolithic cereals, domestic caprines, and Cardial-impressed pottery.
evidence.summary: Stratified cave deposits capture early Northwest African cereal farming and impressed pottery, which ancient genomes show involved migrant Iberian farmers admixing with local Iberomaurusian descendants.
evidence.limits: Eastern Maghreb Neolithic genomes show far higher local forager genetic continuity than northwestern Morocco.

evidence.title: Messak Settafet (Libya): Saharan cattle burial monuments
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on disarticulated cattle and ovicaprid deposits in corbelled stone monuments.
evidence.summary: Groups across the central Saharan plateau built formal stone monuments over sacrificed cattle during late Green Sahara aridification, underscoring social and ritual value of herds.
evidence.limits: Acidic surface soils vary in collagen survival across surveyed plateau monuments.

evidence.title: Gobero (Niger): Tenerian pastoral & complex grave-goods phase
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon determinations on Tenerian skeletal burials and domesticated cattle finds.
evidence.summary: Mid-Holocene return to the Gobero paleolake brought cattle herding, diverse wildlife exploitation, and distinct flexed burials with ornaments before permanent lake desiccation.
evidence.limits: Shared basin coordinate slightly offset from Kiffian marker for legibility.

evidence.title: Faiyum North Shore (Kom W & Kom K): Early Egyptian Neolithic farming
evidence.dateBasis: Reinvestigated stratigraphies and radiocarbon dates on storage pits, sickles, fish bone, and domesticates at Kom W and Kom K.
evidence.summary: Combines the earliest clear Egyptian cereal storage pits (emmer wheat, barley) and Southwest Asian sheep/goats/cattle with continued heavy reliance on Nile and lake fishing.
evidence.limits: Deflated surface lag deposits preserve storage silos and hearths better than perishable dwellings.

evidence.title: Esh-Shaheinab (Central Sudan): Khartoum Neolithic herding & Nile craft
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon chronology and organic residue analysis from Classic Shaheinab Nile bank layers north of Omdurman.
evidence.summary: Shows partial ceramic continuity with earlier Mesolithic Nile fisher-foragers alongside the rapid incorporation of domestic cattle and caprines into a broad savanna-riverine diet.
evidence.limits: Organic residue samples reflect a subset of excavated pottery vessels.

evidence.title: Hierakonpolis (Nekhen, Upper Egypt): Predynastic urban & ritual center
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified settlement cuts, elite cemetery HK6 tombs, and GPR-traced enclosure surveys.
evidence.summary: One of Upper Egypt’s largest Predynastic towns, preserving specialized brewing and pottery kilns, elite cemetery complexes, massive timber-palisaded ritual precincts, and buried prehistoric structures mapped via high-resolution GPR.
evidence.limits: Modern agriculture covers portions of the alluvial plain settlement.

evidence.title: Abydos (Umm el-Qaab Tomb U-j): earliest hieroglyphic tags & early state
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon and ceramic seriation of Cemetery U and Early Dynastic royal tombs at Abydos.
evidence.summary: Elite Tomb U-j at Abydos preserves incised bone and ivory labels with phonetic Egyptian sign values alongside imported Levantine wine jars, marking administrative writing before Dynasty 1.
evidence.limits: Perishable administrative records on papyrus or wood from the earliest phases have not survived.

evidence.title: Tangier Peninsula (NW Morocco): Bronze & Iron Age cemeteries and rock art
evidence.dateBasis: Spatial inventory and typological-radiocarbon chronology of tumuli, cist graves, and shelter art.
evidence.summary: Dense monumental cist cemeteries and painted shelters show active trans-Gibraltar and Saharan-Atlantic interaction long before Phoenician colonies along the Strait.
evidence.limits: Many megalithic monuments were disturbed before modern absolute dating campaigns.

evidence.title: Giza (Heit el-Ghurab & pyramid complex): Old Kingdom supply & town
evidence.dateBasis: Ceramic seriation, sealings, and imported Levantine Combed Ware petrography from Giza pyramid and workers’ settlement contexts.
evidence.summary: Documents both the monumental Old Kingdom pyramid landscape and the adjacent barracks, bakeries, cattle-feasting organization, and Eastern Mediterranean timber-and-oil supply lines at Giza.
evidence.limits: Heit el-Ghurab excavated sectors illuminate Fourth Dynasty labor state organization rather than the entire Memphite city.

evidence.title: Kerma (Third Cataract, Sudan): Capital of Early Kush
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified mud-brick Western Deffufa town sequence and monumental tumulus burials in the Eastern Cemetery.
evidence.summary: Centered upstream of Egypt’s First Cataract, the Kingdom of Kerma built the fortified mud-brick Deffufa temple city, raised massive royal tumuli surrounded by hundreds of cattle bucrania, and controlled Middle Nile gold and exotic trade.
evidence.limits: Royal cemetery chronology relies on ceramic typology, radiocarbon, and Egyptian synchronisms prior to local Kushite writing.

evidence.title: Amarna (Akhetaten, Middle Egypt): Short-lived New Kingdom city
evidence.dateBasis: Historical regnal records on boundary stelae paired with urban house stratigraphy and non-elite cemetery bioarchaeology.
evidence.summary: A single-generation capital built by Akhenaten whose non-elite cemeteries reveal high childhood workload, malnutrition, and disputed bioarchaeological hypotheses regarding a Late Bronze Age epidemic.
evidence.limits: Short occupation window creates a rare snapshot of non-royal urban health alongside royal diplomacy.

evidence.title: Jebel Barkal & Napata (Karima): Heart of the 25th Dynasty & Early Kush
evidence.dateBasis: Royal pyramid cemeteries of El-Kurru and Nuri plus Amun temple foundation deposits beneath Jebel Barkal.
evidence.summary: From Napata below the Fourth Cataract, Kushite kings expanded northward to rule all of Egypt as the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty and maintained steep sandstone pyramid burials at El-Kurru and Nuri.
evidence.limits: Settlement domestic quarters around Jebel Barkal remain less excavated than temples and royal pyramids.

evidence.title: Carthage (Bir Massouda & Magon Quarter): Phoenician-Punic metropolis
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon determinations on foundation deposits, metallurgical smithing layers at Bir Massouda, and Magon Quarter seawall phases.
evidence.summary: Excavations show densely planned seafront urban blocks, North Africa’s earliest dated ferrous smithing workshops, and Mediterranean-wide maritime trade before Roman destruction in 146 BCE.
evidence.limits: Modern suburban Tunis overlies large parts of the Punic town plan.

evidence.title: Royal City of Meroë (Sudan): Kushite capital & monumental ironworking
evidence.dateBasis: Ninety-seven AMS radiocarbon dates on smelting slag heaps, Amun temple phases, and royal pyramids at Begarawiya.
evidence.summary: Capital of the Meroitic Kingdom of Kush featuring distinctive alphabetic Meroitic script, over two hundred steep pyramids, sandstone temples, and massive iron-smelting mounds sustainably fueled by Nile Acacia.
evidence.limits: Iron production spans both Meroitic and post-Meroitic phases with major chronological variability across slag heaps.

evidence.title: Volubilis / Walīla (Morocco): Mauretanian, Roman & Early Islamic town
evidence.dateBasis: Monumental urban inscriptions, oil-press complexes, and modern excavations of the extra-mural early Islamic settlement of Walīla.
evidence.summary: A major Amazigh (Mauretanian) royal city turned Roman olive-oil boomtown, which remained continuously settled and later hosted Idris I’s eighth-century North African state at medieval Walīla.
evidence.limits: Early colonial excavations cleared Roman peristyle houses down to stone without modern stratigraphic recovery.

evidence.title: Leptis Magna (Libya): Punic port turned Tripolitanian Roman metropolis
evidence.dateBasis: Harbor engineering sequences, tri-lingual Punic-Latin-Greek epigraphy, and Tripolitanian rural olive-villa surveys.
evidence.summary: Grew from a Phoenician-Libyan emporium into a monumental Severan port city exporting olive oil and Saharan-linked goods backed by dense hinterland estate surveys.
evidence.limits: Late antique harbour silting and Vandal/Byzantine contraction vary across sectors.

evidence.title: Old Dongola (Sudan): Capital of Christian Makuria & Funj Dongola
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated monastic crypts on Kom H, churches, archaeobotanical cereal assemblages, and Funj-era Arabic administrative letters.
evidence.summary: Served for nearly a millennium as the fortified cathedral and monastic capital of the Christian kingdom of Makuria, then continued as an urban center of the Islamic Funj Sultanate into the early nineteenth century.
evidence.limits: Excavations continue across citadel residential quarters.

evidence.title: Kairouan (Al-Qayrawān, Tunisia): Early Islamic Maghreb capital
evidence.dateBasis: Historical foundation records paired with Aghlabid hydraulic basins, Great Mosque phases, and Medjerda-region ceramics.
evidence.summary: Founded in 670 CE inland from Byzantine coastal fleets, Kairouan became Ifrīqiya’s political capital, hydraulic engineering hub, and North Africa’s premier center of Islamic scholarship before Zirid-Hilalian upheaval in 1057.
evidence.limits: Dense modern historic medina limits deep open-area urban trenching beneath mosques.

evidence.title: Fusṭāṭ & Historic Cairo (Egypt): Nile capital & craft metropolis
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated kiln districts, multi-story domestic courtyards, Geniza community records, and standing Fatimid-Mamluk architecture.
evidence.summary: Emerging from the seventh-century Nilotic town of Fusṭāṭ alongside al-Qāhira (founded 969 CE), Cairo became one of the largest commercial, ceramic, and scholarly capitals linking the Mediterranean, Red Sea, and sub-Saharan caravan worlds.
evidence.limits: High modern density restricts open-area excavation mostly to salvage plots in Istabl Antar and Fusṭāṭ.

evidence.title: Fez / Fès (Morocco): Idrisid & Marinid Maghreb capital
evidence.dateBasis: Marinid madrasa inscriptions, Qarawiyyin architectural sequence, and North African urban jurisprudence surveys.
evidence.summary: Founded at the crossroads of Mediterranean and Saharan routes (including Sijilmasa caravan links), Fez grew under the Idrisids, Almohads, and Marinids into a major craft, leather-tanning, and university city.
evidence.limits: Historical continuity makes subsurface early foundation strata difficult to isolate from later renovations.

evidence.title: Tassili n’Ajjer (Algeria): Round Head & Bovine pastoral rock-art plateau
evidence.dateBasis: Direct radiocarbon and luminescence dates on shelter occupation deposits linked to superimposed Saharan rock paintings and engravings.
evidence.summary: Sandstone canyon shelters across the Tassili plateau preserve thousands of stratified panels transitioning from wild savanna fauna and Round Head figures into Bovine pastoral scenes before Sahara aridification.
evidence.limits: Direct absolute dating of open-air rock pigments remains scarce relative to excavated shelter floors.

evidence.title: Saïs (Sa el-Hagar, Western Nile Delta): Lower Egyptian Neolithic village
evidence.dateBasis: Deep augering and wet-sieved delta settlement trenches below historic Saïs.
evidence.summary: Preserves deeply stratified Western Delta fishing and pig/cattle/cereal village horizons showing indigenous Lower Egyptian agricultural foundations preceding Dynastic unification.
evidence.limits: High Nile groundwater table limits wide lateral exposure of deepest Neolithic layers.

evidence.title: Southern Atbai & Mahal Teglinos (Eastern Sudan): Pastoralism & early sorghum
evidence.dateBasis: Botanical impressions on potsherds, settlement mounds at Mahal Teglinos (Kassala), and radiocarbon chronologies across the Atbai Plains.
evidence.summary: Documents mobile-to-settled Atbai herding communities between the Nile and Red Sea Hills who cultivated early domesticated sorghum alongside regional exchange linking Kerma and the Horn.
evidence.limits: Site preservation favors seasonal camp mounds on raised alluvial fans.

evidence.title: Garama (Jarma, Fezzan, Libya): Capital of the Garamantian oasis state
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations at Old Jarma, subterranean foggara irrigation channels, oasis archaeobotany, and trans-Saharan tomb goods.
evidence.summary: Built an urban Saharan civilization along the Wadi al-Ajal powered by hundreds of kilometers of underground foggara irrigation canals, irrigated date-wheat-cotton oases, iron smithing, and caravan networks connecting Rome with West Africa.
evidence.limits: Late Garamantian shrinkage into medieval Fezzan settlements overlaps with rising aridity and changing aquifer tables.

evidence.title: Dangeil & Fifth Cataract (Sudan): Kushite Amun temple & royal metallurgy
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Amun temple rooms, sacred processional kiosks, and crucibles for specialized tin-bronze casting.
evidence.summary: Regional Fifth Cataract Kushite urban center preserving a monumental sandstone-and-fired-brick Amun temple, elite Kushite funerary practices, and dedicated high-temperature bronze workshops.
evidence.limits: Represents excavated temple and craft sectors of a broader mud-brick urban settlement.

evidence.title: Mecca (Makkah, Hijaz): Sanctuary of the Kaaba & Hajj pilgrimage networks
evidence.dateBasis: Early Islamic Arabic inscriptions from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, Hijaz textual corpora, and Darb Zubaydah / Red Sea pilgrimage road archaeology.
evidence.summary: Inland Hijaz valley housing the Kaaba sanctuary, birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad (c. 570 CE), and focal point of annual Hajj journeys drawing Muslim pilgrims across Africa via Cairo, ʿAydhāb, Suakin, and Jeddah alongside inland Syrian and Iraqi caravan roads.
evidence.limits: Continuous sacred rebuilding around the sanctuary covers deepest pre-seventh-century urban strata.

evidence.title: Medina (Yathrib, Hijaz): The 622 CE Hijrah & early Islamic polity
evidence.dateBasis: Hijri calendar epoch (622 CE), monumental epigraphy, oasis archaeology, and early mosque reconstruction histories.
evidence.summary: Oasis settlement of Yathrib where the 622 CE migration (Hijrah) of Muhammad established the first Muslim community and Constitution of Medina, becoming a primary seat of Prophetic Mosque heritage and scholarly lineages.
evidence.limits: Modern expansion across the oasis restricts subsurface exposure of earliest seventh-century precincts.

evidence.title: Haua Fteah Cave (Cyrenaica, Libya): Epipaleolithic, Capsian & early herders
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian AMS radiocarbon chronology and sediment micromorphology through the upper 5 metres of the Jebel Akhdar karst cavern.
evidence.summary: Deep limestone shelter preserving a continuous eastern Maghreb sequence from Iberomaurusian/Oranian foraging through Libyco-Capsian shell middens into the introduction of domestic sheep/goats and pottery.
evidence.limits: Trench sampling focuses on McBurney and recent Cambridge–University of Tripoli columns inside a cavernous floor.

evidence.title: Kerma–Kawa Middle Nile Corridor: Holocene river avulsion & agrarian continuity
evidence.dateBasis: Fluvial palaeochannel reconstruction combined with multi-site dental morphological biodiversity comparisons across Upper Nubia.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates how shifting Nile distributary channels structured fertile alluvial basins where indigenous hunter-forager populations transitioned into Neolithic and Pre-Kerma cultivators largely through local demographic continuity.
evidence.limits: Sub-surface alluvium obscures smaller ephemeral riverside camps between surveyed palaeochannels.

evidence.title: Gilf Kebir & Wadi Sura (SW Egypt): Mid-Holocene humid Sahara rock shelters
evidence.dateBasis: Geoarchaeological playalake sediments and shelter occupations surrounding the painted panels of Wadi Sura (Caves of Swimmers & Beasts).
evidence.summary: Isolated sandstone plateaus inside the now-hyperarid Libyan Desert hosted seasonal human groups hunting wild savanna game and later herding cattle during Holocene wet phases before aridification drove groups toward the Nile.
evidence.limits: Open-air rock paintings cannot be directly radiocarbon-dated without paint organic binders.

evidence.title: Ennedi Massif & Nabara (NE Chad): Pastoral rock engravings & desert crossroads
evidence.dateBasis: Systematic rock-art documentation at Nabara and canyon guelta shelters across the Ennedi Plateau.
evidence.summary: Permanent canyon waterpools made Ennedi a long-lived ecological refugium linking Chadian Borkou lowlands, Darfur, and Nubia through dense sequences of cattle-herding engravings and painted rock shelters.
evidence.limits: Stylistic sequences rely on superposition and regional Saharan analogies where shelter trenching is sparse.

evidence.title: Merimde Beni Salama (Western Nile Delta, Egypt): Early Delta agricultural town
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified tell levels, mud-brick/posthole oval huts, woven basket-lined grain silos, and Western Delta survey transects.
evidence.summary: One of Lower Egypt’s earliest enduring sedentary villages on the desert margin, pairing cultivated emmer wheat, six-row barley, pigs, sheep, and cattle with intensive Delta fishing and bifacial lithic craft.
evidence.limits: Adjacent Nile floodplain deposits lie deep beneath modern agricultural silt.

evidence.title: Wadi Diib & Atbai Corridor (Sudanese Eastern Desert): Petroglyphic camel-cattle routes
evidence.dateBasis: Systematic survey of dozens of desert rock-art panels mapping highland boats, long-horned cattle, and pastoral trails.
evidence.summary: Maps corridors traversed by Eastern Desert pastoralists connecting the Fifth Cataract Nile Valley with the Red Sea hills and early shipping representations.
evidence.limits: Relative superposition and motif parallels date open sandstone boulders rather than direct AMS determinations.

evidence.title: Tipasa & Numidian Coast (Algeria): Punic emporium, Numidian state & Roman port
evidence.dateBasis: Punic necropolis assemblages, nearby Royal Mausoleum of Mauretania, amphitheater, and early Christian basilica inscriptions.
evidence.summary: Port along the Algerian Tell illustrating cultural convergence among indigenous Amazigh/Numidian royal dynasties, Carthaginian merchants, Roman civic architecture, and thriving fourth-century North African Christian churches.
evidence.limits: Modern coastal erosion affects seafront Roman and Punic port quarters.

evidence.title: Faras & Nobatia / Alwa (Nile Corridor, Sudan): Christian kingdoms & Baqt peace
evidence.dateBasis: Cathedral frescoes rescued from Faras before Lake Nasser flooding, Old Nubian texts, and treaty records of the 652 CE Baqt.
evidence.summary: Byzantine missions in the 540s–580s initiated the kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria, and Alwa, whose churches painted multi-lingual Greek-Coptic-Old Nubian murals and maintained a centuries-long diplomatic Baqt truce with Islamic Egypt.
evidence.limits: Portions of northern Nobatia now lie submerged beneath Lake Nasser, elevating archived UNESCO salvage records.

evidence.title: Tahert, M’zab & Sijilmasa (Maghreb Interior): Ibāḍī imamate & early caravan mints
evidence.dateBasis: Foundational Rustamid/Midrarid chronicles, oasis hydraulic ksour surveys in the M’zab pentapolis, and early Islamic silver/gold trade coinage.
evidence.summary: Amazigh communities adopting Ibāḍī and Ṣufrī scholarship founded northern Saharan-fringe polities at Tahert (776) and Sijilmasa (757), creating early Islamic trans-Saharan trade portals and fortified foggara oasis towns later preserved across the M’zab.
evidence.limits: Medieval Tahert awaits extensive subsurface exposure compared with standing M’zab ksour.

evidence.title: Ancient Ksour of Chinguetti, Ouadane, Tichitt & Oualata (Mauritania): Western Saharan hubs
evidence.dateBasis: Standing dry-stone courtyard-and-mosque urban plans paired with Arabic manuscript libraries across Mauritanian Adrar and Hodh caravan towns.
evidence.summary: After Sijilmasa and Aoudaghost, stone-built fortified ksour in Chinguetti, Ouadane and Oualata anchored western trans-Saharan caravans carrying Taoudenni/Idjil rock salt, manuscripts and gold between Morocco and the Niger–Senegal valleys.
evidence.limits: Sub-surface stratigraphic excavations under active oasis compounds remain far rarer than architectural and manuscript surveys.

evidence.title: Historic Centre of Agadez (Aïr Massif, Niger): Tuareg sultanate & earthen mosque crossroads
evidence.dateBasis: Urban archaeology syntheses of Saharan oasis urbanization paired with the fifteenth–sixteenth-century Sultanate of Aïr, palace quarter and iconic 27-metre earthen minaret.
evidence.summary: Situated along the southern Aïr edge facing Hausaland, Takedda/Azelik copper mines and Kawar/Bilma salt pans, Agadez organized confederated Tuareg caravan logistics connecting Kano and Gao to Ghat and Tripoli.
evidence.limits: Timber-reinforced banco repairs regularly renew visible earthen superstructures.

evidence.title: Old Town of Ghadamès & Zuwīla (Libyan Sahara): Ibāḍī oasis markets & Fezzan caravan axis
evidence.dateBasis: Oasis excavations at Fezzan Zuwīla combined with UNESCO architectural surveys of Ghadamès’s covered adobe streetways and subterranean oasis springs.
evidence.summary: Bridging Tripolitania and Ifriqiya to Ghat, Kawar and Bornu, the walled oasis towns of Ghadamès and Zuwīla combined climate-adapted shaded arcades, spring irrigation and mercantile brokerage between North African and central Sudanic merchants.
evidence.limits: Political instability and dune encroachment limit ongoing stratified fieldwork across southern Libya.

evidence.title: Touat, Gourara & Tidikelt Oases (Adrar, Algerian Sahara): Subterranean foggara hydraulics
evidence.dateBasis: Hydrological and urban studies of underground foggara infiltration galleries paired with Wadi Draa and Tafilalt trans-Saharan oasis chronologies.
evidence.summary: Networks of gently sloped underground foggara channels tapped continental aquifers across western Algeria to sustain fortified ksour, date-palm agro-ecosystems and scholarly stops along the Sijilmasa–Timbuktu route.
evidence.limits: Repeatedly cleared underground tunnels rarely preserve primary construction organics undisturbed.

evidence.title: Soba East (Blue Nile, Sudan): Medieval churches & urban diversity of the Kingdom of Alwa
evidence.dateBasis: Non-invasive geophysical magnetometry across 275 hectares of mud/fired-brick mounds paired with skeletal strontium/dietary isotope studies of Alwan residents.
evidence.summary: Southernmost of the three Christian Nubian kingdoms, Soba East spanned massive fired-brick churches, palaces and artisanal workshops near the Blue–White Nile confluence before the 1504 CE rise of the Funj Sultanate.
evidence.limits: Suburban expansion of greater Khartoum threatens outer unexcavated mounds of the historic site.

evidence.title: Sennar & the Funj Kingdom (Blue Nile, Sudan): al-Salṭana al-Zarqāʾ & Nilotic-Red Sea Islamization
evidence.dateBasis: Archaeological charters and Arabic correspondence from Old Dongola/Sennar, Funj palace histories and Ṭabaqāt chronicles of Sudanese Islamic scholars.
evidence.summary: Centered on Sennar from 1504 to 1821, the Funj Sultanate knitted together Nubian Christian-heritage riverlands, Beja Eastern Desert clans and Islamic khalwa centers from the Third Cataract to the Ethiopian borderlands.
evidence.limits: Old Sennar ruins were heavily damaged by twentieth-century river erosion and reservoir works.

evidence.title: Qasr Ibrim (Lower Nubia, Egypt): Cliff-top cathedral, Nubian archives & Ottoman garrison
evidence.dateBasis: Arid-preserved Old Nubian, Arabic and Ottoman Turkish leather/paper manuscripts paired with historical archaeology of Bosnian-Ottoman garrison houses on the island promontory.
evidence.summary: High above the flooded Nile valley, Qasr Ibrim preserves an extraordinary continuous archive spanning late Christian Nubian bishoprics, Mamluk frontier diplomacy and sixteenth-to-nineteenth-century Ottoman garrisons.
evidence.limits: Lake Nasser flooding left only the highest citadel plateau above water since the 1960s.

evidence.title: Uri, Ain Farah & Jebel Marra (Darfur, Western Sudan): Stone citadels & the Keira Sultanate
evidence.dateBasis: Architectural surveys of dry-stone Tora compounds and Ain Farah fired-brick mosques paired with Keira royal charters and the Darb al-Arbaʿīn caravan history.
evidence.summary: Dry-stone fortified compounds in northern Darfur (Uri, Ain Farah, Shoba) chart state consolidation under Daju, Tunjur and the Keira Fur Sultanate (which controlled the Forty Days Road from Kobbei to Upper Egypt until 1874 and revived briefly in 1898).
evidence.limits: Modern conflict has severely restricted stratigraphic excavation and radiocarbon refinement across Darfur.

evidence.title: Suakin & ʿAydhāb (Red Sea Coast, Sudan/Egypt): Medieval Hajj port & Ottoman coral island
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations at coral-built Ottoman Suakin (1517/1555–1865 Ottoman province to Khedivial port) and medieval ʿAydhāb pilgrim harbor.
evidence.summary: First ʿAydhāb (until the fifteenth century) and then Suakin island served as Africa’s primary Red Sea embarkation ports facing Jeddah and Mecca, uniting Nubian–Beja caravans, Indian Ocean Gujarat–Yemen shipping and Ottoman-Red Sea trade.
evidence.limits: Coral-rag buildings at Suakin suffer rapid salt-weathering collapse since the early twentieth-century shift to Port Sudan.

evidence.title: Medina of Marrakesh (Morocco): Almoravid foundation, Almohad mosques & Saadian palaces
evidence.dateBasis: Historical-archaeological studies of Almoravid foundation c. 1070 CE, underground khettara aqueducts, Almohad Kutubiyya Mosque and sixteenth-century Saadian El Badi / tombs.
evidence.summary: Founded at the High Atlas northern gateway by Sanhaja Almoravids, Marrakesh united Saharan–Sudanic gold networks with Andalusian hydraulic and architectural craft under the Almoravid, Almohad, Saadian and Alaouite dynasties.
evidence.limits: Medieval domestic levels frequently underlie dense historic medina residential blocks.

evidence.title: Rabat (Ribāṭ al-Fatḥ), Chellah & Tinmel (Morocco): Almohad Atlantic port & Marinid necropolis
evidence.dateBasis: Almohad imperial wall and Hassan Tower construction records (1195–1199), numismatic evidence, Marinid Chellah excavations and seventeenth-century Bou Regreg maritime archives.
evidence.summary: From High Atlas cradle Tinmel to the monumental Atlantic citadel at Ribāṭ al-Fatḥ (Rabat), the Almohad movement built an empire spanning the Maghreb and al-Andalus before later hosting Marinid necropolises and the seventeenth-century Republic of Bou Regreg.
evidence.limits: Continuous urban rebuilding along the Bou Regreg estuary modifies earlier Almohad quay shorelines.

evidence.title: Ksar of Ait-Ben-Haddou & Wadi Draa Oases (Southern Morocco): Rammed-earth Saharan gateways
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified oasis town survey across Wadi Draa combined with UNESCO pisé earth-and-timber ksar conservation studies in the Ounila Valley.
evidence.summary: Positioned along the High Atlas Ounila and Draa valleys descending from Marrakesh toward the Sahara, fortified earthen ksour (Ait-Ben-Haddou) sheltered communal granaries, date gardens and trans-Atlas merchant caravans.
evidence.limits: Most surviving standing towers date to the seventeenth–nineteenth centuries over older pre-Saharan valley settlements.

evidence.title: Qalʿat Banī Ḥammād & Zayyanid Tlemcen (Algeria): Highland fortress & Central Maghreb capital
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Hammadid palace complexes in the Hodna Mountains (1007–1152 CE) paired with Mechouar citadel and Yaʿqūbiyya architectural records in Zayyanid Tlemcen (1236–1554 CE).
evidence.summary: After Sanhaja Hammadids built high-mountain palaces and glazed-tile courts at Qalʿat Banī Ḥammād, Zayyanid Tlemcen linked Oran Mediterranean shipping directly with Sijilmasa and central Saharan caravans until Ottoman integration.
evidence.limits: Modern Tlemcen overlays portions of the outer medieval suburban workshops.

evidence.title: Hafsid Tunis & Ottoman Kasbah of Algiers (Tunisia/Algeria): Maghreb capitals & Mediterranean fleets
evidence.dateLabel: 1229–1900 CE (Hafsid to Ottoman Regency & French protectorate/colonial)
evidence.dateBasis: Ifriqiya urban-architectural studies, Hafsid court ceremonies and surveys of the sixteenth-to-nineteenth-century Ottoman sea fortifications and Kasbah of Algiers.
evidence.summary: From the 1229 Hafsid Sultanate in Tunis (welcoming Iberian Andalusi scholars and Genoese/Venetian fondacos) to the 1516 Ottoman Regencies of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli, North African port capitals anchored Mediterranean diplomacy and trans-Saharan commerce to 1900.
evidence.limits: Colonial nineteenth-century marine boulevard reconstructions altered Lower Kasbah harbourfronts.

evidence.title: Wadi Kubbaniya (Upper Egypt): Terminal Pleistocene wild tuber grinding & Nile flood foraging
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/AMS-dated Nile seasonal floodplain dunes preserving charred purple-nut-grass tubers, grinding stones and Tilapia fish traps.
evidence.summary: Fill Africa’s arid Last Glacial Maximum Nile window: seasonal hunter-fisher-foragers along Wadi Kubbaniya intensively ground toxic wild sedge tubers and preserved catfishes on floodplain margins.
evidence.limits: Wild Nile flood fluctuations periodically truncated shallow dune camp horizons.

evidence.title: Afalou Bou Rhummel (Kabylie, Algeria): Iberomaurusian cliff-shelter necropolis & baked clay figurines
evidence.dateBasis: Direct radiocarbon dates on multiple collective Iberomaurusian burials, backed bladelets and rare fired-terracotta zoomorphic figurines.
evidence.summary: Alongside Taforalt, Afalou anchors Late Pleistocene coastal Maghreb continuity where Mechta–Afalou communities practiced tooth evulsion, fired clay animal art and collective burial.
evidence.limits: 1920s–1930s trenching removed sections of upper Capsian-transitional overburden.

evidence.title: Elkab & Esna Nile Floodplains (Upper Egypt): Terminal Pleistocene to Early Holocene lithic transitions
evidence.dateBasis: Late Paleolithic bladelet–backed-point assemblages and post-Younger Dryas Elkabian fishing camps embedded in Nile silt terraces.
evidence.summary: Bridges the volatile "Wild Nile" floods and Younger Dryas arid interval into Early Holocene Nile Epipaleolithic fisher-forager settlements prior to Saharan monsoonal lake expansion.
evidence.limits: Alluvial erosion along the incised Nile bank limits continuous vertical profiles between Esna and Elkab.

evidence.title: Tamar Hat & Abri Alain (Algerian Tell): Late Glacial Barbary-sheep & marine-mollusk foraging
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Iberomaurusian Barbary sheep (Ammotragus) faunal sequences and malacofaunal coastal shell exploitation across northern Algeria.
evidence.summary: Documents specialized Mediterranean Atlas coastal foraging balancing rocky-mountain Barbary sheep hunting with seasonal intertidal shellfish collection through the terminal Pleistocene.
evidence.limits: Submerged continental shelves hide lowland winter camps below modern sea level.

evidence.title: Ounjougou (Bandiagara Escarpment, Mali): Tenth-millennium Early Holocene West African pottery
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/AMS dates on incised hemispherical sherds, leaf-shaped bifacial points, grinding stones and Sahelian wild-grass phytoliths.
evidence.summary: Establishes the Yamé valley at Ounjougou as one of Africa’s independent Early Holocene hearths of ceramic invention, coinciding with returning monsoonal savannas for processing wild grains.
evidence.limits: Intensive seasonal Yamé gully incisions fragment horizontal open-camp plans.

evidence.title: Al-Khiday & Kabbashi Haitah (White & Main Nile, Sudan): Semi-sedentary fisher-potters
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated shell-mound middens, wavy-line dotted ceramics, bone harpoons, Nile fish–turtle faunal assemblages and Pre-Mesolithic graves.
evidence.summary: Documents dense Early-to-Mid-Holocene semi-sedentary Nile villages in central Sudan harvesting wild panicoid seeds, lungfish and mammals alongside specialized petrographic pottery traditions.
evidence.limits: Meroitic and post-Meroitic grave intrusions cut upper Mesolithic mound surfaces at Al-Khiday.

evidence.title: Tadrart Acacus Shelters (Fezzan, Libya): Early Saharan plant-processing pots & monumental murals
evidence.dateBasis: Lipid-residue chromatography confirming cooked C3/C4 wild aquatic plants in 8200–6400 BCE pots alongside Round Head–Pastoral rock paintings (UNESCO WHC 287).
evidence.summary: Provides the oldest direct biomolecular proof of leafy-plant and cereal cooking in ceramic vessels globally within painted Green Sahara sandstone massifs spanning hunters, herders and charioteers.
evidence.limits: Salt weathering and wind abrasion selectively erode exposed shelter pigments.

evidence.title: Khor Shambat 1 (Omdurman, Sudan): Mesolithic-to-Neolithic Nile biological & burial shifts
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Neolithic pot-burials, cattle-sheep pastoral shifts and dental-biological analyses connecting Khartoum Mesolithic and Predynastic Nile traditions.
evidence.summary: Clarifies Middle Nile cultural convergence between indigenous foraging-fishing communities and incoming domesticated herd pastoralists during fifth-millennium arid pulses.
evidence.limits: Urban expansion across modern Omdurman confines remaining mound intactness.

evidence.title: Memphis, Saqqara, Abusir & Dahshur (Lower Egypt): Old-to-New Kingdom pyramid fields
evidence.dateBasis: Djoser’s Step Pyramid limestone masonry, Dahshur–Abusir sun temples and satellite–borehole reconstructions of the Ahramat paleochannel (UNESCO WHC 86).
evidence.summary: Traces Egyptian royal stone-masonry engineering, Memphite necropolis state workshops and Nile floodplain adaptation across three millennia along the desert-edge capital corridor.
evidence.limits: Alluvial urbanization over the eastern Memphite city mound masks secular palace districts compared to desert tombs.

evidence.title: Ancient Thebes, Karnak & Valley of the Kings (Upper Egypt): New Kingdom imperial sacred city
evidence.dateBasis: Fluvial core reconstructions along Luxor’s West Bank, Amun temple processional alignments and geological mapping of rock-cut royal hypogea (UNESCO WHC 87).
evidence.summary: Pairs Karnak and Luxor’s evolving Nile-bar religious complexes on the east bank with artisans’ Deir el-Medina village and painted New Kingdom royal tombs on the west bank.
evidence.limits: Ancient flash flooding in the Valley of the Kings periodically damaged painted limestone sarcophagi.

evidence.title: Abu Simbel, Philae & Lower Nubian Monuments (Egypt–Sudan Border): Sacred river-gateway temples
evidence.dateBasis: Ramesside cliff sanctuaries relocated under UNESCO’s international salvage campaign (WHC 88), Isis sanctuary at Philae and Holocene Nubian Nile dynamics.
evidence.summary: Documents nearly two millennia of Egyptian–Kushite–Ptolemaic–Roman sacred architecture along the First–Second Cataract corridor, closing Philae’s last hieroglyphic inscription in 394 CE.
evidence.limits: Nasser Reservoir inundation drowned non-relocated river-terrace villages beneath Lake Nubia.

evidence.title: Timgad, Sabratha, Cyrene & Tipasa (North Africa): Punic–Numidian–Roman municipal cities
evidence.dateBasis: Decumanus–cardo orthogonal grids at Timgad (WHC 191), Sabratha theater reliefs (WHC 184), Tipasa surveys and Cyrene Doric–Roman sanctuaries (WHC 19).
evidence.summary: Demonstrates North Africa’s extraordinary urban density from Greek Cyrenaica and Punic-Berber emporia to Imperial Roman olive-and-grain provinces before Vandal and Byzantine transitions.
evidence.limits: Antiquarian monumental clearance often removed late antique–Islamic reuse layers across civic forums.

waves.title: Green Sahara pastoral & dairying networks
waves.summary: During the African Humid Period, cattle and caprine herding along with milking traditions expanded unevenly across Saharan paleolakes and savanna corridors before Sahelian shifts after ~3000 BCE.
waves.limits: Schematic arc joining dated archaeozoological and lipid-residue horizons rather than a continuous migration highway.

waves.title: Trans-Saharan caravan & urban corridor
waves.summary: Camel-borne desert crossings linked North African markets like Fez and Sijilmasa through Entrepôts such as Essouk-Tadmekka to Gao, Timbuktu, and the Inland Niger Delta for gold, salt, copper, textiles, and manuscripts.
waves.limits: Representative caravan corridor; multiple parallel western and central routes shifted across centuries.

waves.title: Trans-Saharan Caravan Networks: Maghreb–Oases–Sudan Corridors (c. 1000–1890 CE)
waves.dateBasis: Oasis archaeology at Sijilmasa/Draa/Chinguetti/Ghadamès/Zuwīla/Agadez paired with Arabic and Bornu-Maghreb diplomatic archives.
waves.summary: Schematic western and central trans-Saharan camel caravan corridors exchanging gold, salt slabs, Arabic manuscripts, textiles, horses and kola across fortified oasis relays.
waves.limits: Corridor lines connect key oasis stations rather than plotting every shifting dune well or seasonal shortcut.
